finding.observed: each member rendered as THREE stacked fragments (initials badge, then a name/mode stack, then a state badge) instead of one row.
finding.appRule: `_RowView` computes `need = max(child minimum widths)` — metric 96, progress 140, text/badge 160, nested layout/list 200 — then `columns = clamp(floor((width + gap) / (need + gap)), 1, children.length)`. The member row's stack child is a nested layout (200), so at ~300 px it gets ONE column and every child takes its own line.
finding.fix: the roster is now ONE `list` per member: title `DW · Deep Worker` (initials first, so the badge's meaning survives as text), the state word as `trailing`, `tone` for the semantic colour, NO subtitle. A list item cannot wrap into fragments, so each member is exactly one line.
finding.test: “member rows are ONE line each: initials+name as the title, the state WORD as trailing (repair T19)” — asserts no subtitle, a non-empty trailing word, the exact `DW · Deep Worker` title, AND that the tree contains no `row` node at all
